title: Schwab API Limits
author: PricklyPicklePicker
selftext:
Trading manually at Schwab, I began utilizing an options strategy that relies on many small trades per day.  Quickly learned that 390 orders/day was the limit before they'd designate me as a professional and my fill priority dropped to 0.  To better manage the number of trades and allow myself to perform my day job, I got Schwab developer access and had an agent turn my strategy into code that trades for me.  Now I'm receiving the professional designation every time I turn the bot on, not because of the Rule of 390, but for "professional-like activity".  I tried every tweak I can think of to adjust the activity, but at the end of the day, those orders are coming from the API and not a human.

  
Once I'm released from this designation again, I intend to restart manually at some level with agent support.  Gotta get back to the gravy days.

Does anyone have experience with Schwab severely restricting their AI/code?  They gave me API access, they can't be surprised I am using it!

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
Afaik the 390 count is about the orders themselves, averaged over the month, not about how you send them. So the API doesn't really change anything, the bot just gets there faster.

Fewer, bigger orders and less cancel/replace (I think replaces count too) is probably the only real way under it.

replies.author: PricklyPicklePicker
replies.body: The bot is fewer cancels, etc. Too efficient and professional!

replies.author: Good_Ride_2508
replies.body:
Exceeding an average of **390 option orders per day** in a calendar month triggers the industry-standard **390 Professional Orders Rule** (often called the "390 Rule") across U.S. options exchanges

It says only options 390/day or above in a month.

replies.author: PricklyPicklePicker
replies.body: But Schwab has expanded that rule at their brokerage.

comments.author: AlgoTradingQuant
comments.body: I moved to TradeStation for this very reason.

replies.author: PricklyPicklePicker
replies.body:
Were you able to verify Schwab was treating your API orders differently? Everyone I talk to is surprised I am getting docked at less than 390.

Thanks for the TradeStation mention.  How long have you been there? No trouble?

replies.author: Jason_Steakcum
replies.body: Also, can’t execute futures or futures options orders via Schwab API apparently

comments.author: Jason_Steakcum
comments.body:
Surely fees are gonna eat you alive if you’re not a market maker doing that quantity of orders

Schwab should be giving you discounts if you’re doing this many options orders a month:

Volume based options fees  
5k contracts/mo  
.30 + free to close under .65  
10k contracts /mo  
.20 - .25 + free to close under .65  
Better margin rates, etc

I’ve never come close to hitting the limits but I use an options trading platform that connects via their API and the limit seems to be 100 orders a day, any number of contracts. Stop and OTO orders don’t count, cancel and replace orders don’t count, just filled entry orders.

replies.author: EOJ_me
replies.body: That volume based discounts would make a difference.. Interesting your platform only counts filled entry orders and excludes stops and replacements

comments.author: EOJ_me
comments.body: try contact their compliance or API support tem to clarify this since having API access should at least come with clear guidelines on its permitted use
